summary.en: Salvadoran forces have intensified their offensive in Haiti, killing gang leader Mathias Saintil and destroying the mansion of a 400‑member Mawozo gang leader, while President Bukele warned Haitian gang leaders that his troops will finish them as in El Salvador. Haitian leader is traveling to El Salvador to discuss the Salvadoran offensive, and four Salvadoran technicians disappeared after an ambush, prompting Bukele to deploy 2,500 troops. Amnesty International urged that the deployment respect human rights, and the conflict produced 193 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Salvadoranske styrker har økt offensiven i Haiti, drept gjengleder Mathias Saintil og ødelagt herskapshuset til en 400 medlem Mawozo-gjengleder, mens president Bukele advarte haitiske gjengledere om at hans tropper vil fullføre dem som i El Salvador. Den haitiske lederen reiser til El Salvador for å diskutere den salvadoranske offensiven, og fire salvadoranske teknikere forsvant etter et bakholdsangrep, noe som fikk Bukele til å sette inn 2 500 tropper. Amnesty International oppfordret til at innsetningen respekterer menneskerettighetene, og konflikten førte til 193 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
